findings.title: async forEach callback leaves calendar deletion untracked and un-caught
findings.body: `forEach(async ...)` now awaits `getCalendar` (a dynamic import) before `deleteEvent` is called. forEach ignores the returned promises, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch a rejection, and code after the loop runs before any deletion has started. Before, `deleteEvent` was at least invoked synchronously. If the process finishes the request first, such as on serverless, the external calendar event is never deleted, and no error or log shows it. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` (or use `for...of`). The same pattern is in `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125` and `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125`.

findings.title: Dynamic imports start eagerly, so nothing is lazy
findings.body: Each `import(...)` runs when the module is evaluated, so every app is still loaded at startup, just asynchronously. Every call site now needs `await` for no gain. A rejected import also becomes an unhandled rejection at load time. If lazy loading is the goal, use a map of `() => import(...)` thunks. Otherwise keep the static imports.

summary: The change makes `getCalendar` and the app-store lookups async, and the call sites I read all await them. `getCalendarCredentials` stores the promise and `getConnectedCalendars` awaits it, which works. Two issues remain. The `forEach(async ...)` loops in the reschedule code can start calendar deletions after the request has moved on. The eager `import()` calls in `index.ts` give no lazy loading. I did not trace the other callers of `getCalendarCredentials` beyond a grep.
